response.overview: The film introduces viewers to Ludwigslust, the “Pearl of Mecklenburg.” The town was founded in the second half of the 18th century as the residence of a small-town potentate. They wanted—and needed—to make a grand impression, but had no money. The subjects had to come up with a solution, and so the first “synthetic material”—papier-mâché—was perfected to the highest degree and used as a substitute for stucco, woodcarvings, and wrought ironwork, as well as to create durable replicas of sculptural works. Among other things, a Venus de’ Medici served as a model.
response.title: Ludwigs-LUST - Kulturhistorische Randnotizen
